verifications.reason: Multiple independent sources confirm Anadarko and Eni were awarded their Rovuma Basin exploration licenses (Area 1 and Area 4 respectively, offshore northern Mozambique) in 2006, not 2008. title: Dock Workers Strike in Lourenco Marques Suppressed
reason: No independent source corroborates a 1956 dock workers' strike in Lourenço Marques, Mozambique. The well-documented 1956 dock-workers' strike matching this description (workers demanding higher wages, colonial police intervention, arrests) occurred instead in Bissau, Portuguese Guinea (the Casa Gouveia strike of 6 March 1956, per Wikipedia's Pidjiguiti Massacre article) — a different country in the Portuguese empire, not Mozambique. Meanwhile, the actual event matching this description almost verbatim for Lourenço Marques (Mozambique) — African dock/stevedore workers demanding higher wages and better conditions, violently suppressed by Portuguese colonial police with arrests/deportations of leaders, described as one of the first major manifestations of African labor resistance in colonial Mozambique — is the 28 August 1933 'Greve dos Quinhentos' (Strike of the Five Hundred) at the Port of Lourenço Marques (corroborated by a JSTOR-indexed academic article 'Labor Struggles at the Port of Lourenço Marques, 1900-1933' and secondary summaries). No source places a comparable significant dock strike in Lourenço Marques in 1956. Given country=Mozambique is fixed for this file, the year 1956 does not check out; the material description best matches a real Mozambican event dated 1933.
